lines.text: A very long password can log you in to some Linux servers, with no real password.
Linux marks accounts that have no password with a single asterisk.
lines.title: The no-password mark

lines.text: On musl, a password over 256 bytes makes the check fail with an error. The error is also an asterisk.
lines.title: The mix-up

lines.text: OpenSSH sees two asterisks match and lets the attacker in.
lines.title: Login accepted

lines.text: Only some setups are affected. Servers using glibc or PAM are not.
lines.title: Who is at risk

lines.text: Update OpenSSH to ten point six p two, or turn off password logins.
lines.title: What to do
